memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Moses also took all the fat around the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, and both kidneys and their fat, and burned it on the altar. But the bull with its hide and its flesh and its intestines he burned up outside the camp, as the LORD commanded Moses." - Lev 8:16-17 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The best parts rise to God on the altar. Everything else is carried out beyond the boundary and burned.

We have seen this before, and Hebrews has already told us where it points: Jesus also suffered outside the city gate to make the people holy through his own blood (Heb 13:12).

But notice the detail here. This happened at the very start of Aaron's ministry. Before a single day of priestly service, something was carried outside the camp on his behalf.

The ministry began with a death.

That is true of every genuine work for God. Jesus said, Unless a kernel of wheat falls to the ground and dies, it remains only a single seed. But if it dies, it produces many seeds (Jn 12:24). Paul wrote, I have been crucified with Christ and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me (Gal 2:20).

Something has to be taken outside the camp before we are much use inside it. Usually it is our reputation, our preferences, our need to be seen as capable.

That is not a loss to grieve. It is the beginning of fruitfulness.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What in me needs to be carried outside the camp before God can use me freely?
2. Am I willing to lose standing or comfort for the sake of Christ?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, take outside the camp whatever in me hinders Your work. I would rather be fruitful than comfortable. Amen.
